surprises.head: Carolina hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Carolina usually hits more than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 49 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 107 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: The Hurricanes keep the Canucks winless in eight
paras: Juuso Välimäki made his Hurricanes debut, after playing for the Mammoth, and picked up an assist. It was a busy first period. Logan Stankoven struck first for the Hurricanes early in the period, but Linus Karlsson tied it up for Vancouver midway through the period. Nikolaj Ehlers put the Hurricanes up 2-1 just under two minutes later. Jonathan Lekkerimäki made it 2-2 for Vancouver on the power play with just 2 seconds left in the first. Nicolas Deslauriers put the Canes up 3-2 early in the second. Max Sasson made it 3-3 for Vancouver midway through the period, but that’s where Vancouver’s luck ran out. Leevi Meriläinen stopped Sebastian Aho on a penalty shot late in the period. Deslauriers struck again early in the third to put the Hurricanes ahead 4-3, and Ehlers struck again midway through the period to make it 5-3. Stankoven struck again into the empty net with just over two minutes left. There were two three-point nights: Ehlers with two goals and an assist, and Stankoven with two goals and an assist.

The Hurricanes earned this one. Replay the chances a hundred times and they win about seven in ten. Pyotr Kochetkov made 14 saves for the Hurricanes. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Jackson Blake, by our Swing measure. The Hurricanes moved to 8-2-1. The Canucks are winless in eight (0-7-1).

items.text: Andrei Svechnikov’s five-game point streak against Vancouver ended.
The Hurricanes have beaten the Canucks six straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
The Hurricanes have won eight of their last ten.
Nicolas Deslauriers scored his first two goals of the season, his first since Apr 13, 2025 (38 games played since).
